objectives.text: Given necessary information about a system, CALCULATE the work performed and/or power produced or used by that system.

enabling.text: For a mechanical system, CALCULATE energy, work, and power.
STATE the First Law of Thermodynamics, "Conservation of Energy."

passages.quote: Energy is defined as the measure of the ability to do work.
Transient energy is energy in motion, that is, energy being transferred from one place to another.
Stored energy is the energy contained within a substance or object.
referred to as transient energy or, more commonly in the case of thermal energy, heat.
Potential energy is defined as the energy stored in an object because of its position.
Kinetic energy is defined as the energy stored in an object because of its motion.
the g c is used only when using the English system of measurement.
Internal energy is the energy stored in a substance because of the motion and position of the particles of the substance.
Transient mechanical energy is commonly referred to as work.
Work is done by a force acting on a moving object if the object has some component of motion in the direction of the force.
if no movement is achieved, no work has been accomplished.
energy cannot be created or destroyed, only altered in form.
Any energy balance is a statement of the Law of Conservation of Energy.
Power is defined as the amount of energy used per unit time or rate of doing work.
Thermal power is the measure of thermal energy used per unit time.
Mechanical power is the rate at which work is done.
One horsepower is equivalent to 550 ft-lbf/s and 745.7 watts.

body.text: Energy determines the capacity of a system to perform work and may be stored in various forms.
Both thermal and mechanical energy can be separated into two categories, transient and stored.
Thermal energy is related to temperature: the higher the temperature, the greater the molecular movement and the greater the energy. Thermal energy in motion is commonly called heat.
Stored mechanical energy exists in one of two forms, kinetic or potential.

checks.q: What is thermal energy in motion commonly called?
checks.x: Energy moving from one place to another is transient energy. In the case of thermal energy, it is more commonly called heat.

body.text: The measure of an object's position is its vertical distance above a reference point. Its potential energy represents the work required to elevate it to that position from the reference point.
PE = mgz / gc
PE is in ft-lbf, m is mass in lbm, g is 32.17 ft/sec², gc is 32.17 (lbm-ft)/(lbf-sec²), and z is height above a reference in ft.
KE = mv² / 2gc
KE is in ft-lbf, m is mass in lbm, v is velocity in ft/sec, and gc is 32.17 (lbm-ft)/(lbf-sec²).
An object's kinetic energy represents the energy required to increase its velocity from rest to its final velocity.

checks.q: A body's energy is stored because of its position. What type of energy is this?
checks.x: Potential energy is defined as the energy stored in an object because of its position.

checks.q: Which expression gives kinetic energy in English units?
checks.x: KE = mv² / 2gc. The expression mgz / gc is potential energy, and the others are power.

checks.q: What is the potential energy of a 20 lbm object held 10 feet above the ground?
checks.x: PE = mgz / gc = (20 lbm)(32.17 ft/sec²)(10 ft) / 32.17 = 200 ft-lbf.

body.text: W = F x d
W is work done in ft-lbf, F is the force applied in lbf, and d is the distance the object is moved in ft.
Even if you feel fatigued, no work has been done if nothing moved.

checks.q: A constant force of 300 lbf is applied to a box, but the box does not move. How much work is done?
o: It depends on how long the force is applied
checks.x: W = F x d = 300 lbf x 0 ft = 0 ft-lbf. If no movement is achieved, no work has been accomplished.

checks.q: A horizontal force of 100 lbf moves a box 6 feet horizontally. How much work is done?
checks.x: W = F x d = 100 lbf x 6 ft = 600 ft-lbf.

body.text: The First Law of Thermodynamics is simply stated:
The energy expended in raising an object equals the potential energy it gains because of its height.
Energy(initial) + Energy(added) - Energy(removed) = Energy(final)
Neglecting heat, the balance can be written with work terms alone. This simplified energy balance applies only to mechanical problems.
KE1 + PE1 + Won = KE2 + PE2 + Wby

checks.q: How is the First Law of Thermodynamics simply stated?
o: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only altered in form
Energy always flows from high to low temperature
Energy is lost whenever work is done
checks.x: The First Law of Thermodynamics is simply stated: energy cannot be created or destroyed, only altered in form.

body.text: Thermal power is the rate of heat transfer or heat flow rate, calculated as heat used divided by time required.
Mechanical power is expressed in joules/sec or watts in the mks system, and in ft-lbf/s or horsepower in the English system.
P = work done / time required
P = Fd / t
P (hp) = Fv / 550
These equations assume force and velocity are constant, or that average values are used.

checks.q: With force in lbf and velocity in ft/s, which expression gives power in horsepower?
checks.x: P = Fv / 550, because one horsepower is equivalent to 550 ft-lbf/s.

checks.q: A steady force of 100 lbf moves an object at a constant 11 ft/s. What is the power in horsepower?

examples.title: Power of a pump
examples.problem: A pump does 1.5 x 10⁸ ft-lbf of work every 100 minutes. What is the power of the pump in hp?
steps: P = (1.5 x 10⁸ ft-lbf / 100 min)(1 min / 60 sec)(1 hp / 550 ft-lbf/sec).

examples.problem: A steady force of 1 lbf gives a ball a constant velocity of 5 ft/s. What is the power used?

facts.q: What are the two categories of thermal and mechanical energy?

facts.a: The energy stored in a substance because of the motion and position of the particles of the substance.

facts.q: What is transient mechanical energy commonly called?
How many ft-lbf/s and watts equal one horsepower?

facts.a: The measure of thermal energy used per unit time.
The rate at which work is done.

summary.text: Energy is the ability to do work.
The work done by a force on an object is the product of the force and the distance the object moves in the direction of the force.
Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because of its motion. Potential energy is the energy of an object due to its position.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only altered in form.
Power is the amount of energy used per unit time.

The handbook lists Btu as a unit of power and of thermal power, although it defines power as energy per unit time. The lesson does not repeat those units.
Equation number 5-6 is used twice, on pages 7 and 9. The lesson does not use equation numbers.
